finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::no lower bound on `issuedat`: an epoch-zero / far-past timestamp silently drops the edit
evidence: Verified against the supplied source: `yorkie-event.controller.ts` clamps only the upper bound (`Math.min(issuedMs, now)`) and only special-cases `NaN`, so a parseable epoch-zero or Go-zero `issuedAt` yields an `at` far in the past; `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt`'s `where: { id, updatedAt: { lt: at } }` then matches no rows and the discarded `count` plus the unconditional `{ ok: true }` make the drop silent. The claimed inconsistency is also accurate — `parseTimestamp` in `yorkie-admin.service.ts` rejects `ms <= 0` as Yorkie's "unset" value, so the codebase itself assumes that value can arrive. I could not verify from the Yorkie side whether the event webhook ever emits an unset `issuedAt`, so this may be defensive hardening rather than an observed failure; impact per occurrence is one missed `updatedAt` advance (self-healing on the next valid event), hence minor, though it would be major if Yorkie systematically sent zero timestamps.
